src.q: The delivered dose is 2.5 microgram tiotropium per puff (2 puffs comprise one medicinal dose)

brandPrescribing.t: SPS: tiotropium capsules, cartridges and administration devices should be prescribed by brand name, so patients receive an inhaler they have been trained to use.

src.q: To ensure patients receive an inhaler they have been trained to use, tiotropium capsules, cartridges and administration devices should be prescribed by brand name.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: COPD: maintenance bronchodilator to relieve symptoms.

src.q: is indicated as a maintenance bronchodilator treatment to relieve symptoms of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

items.t: Asthma (6 years and over): add-on maintenance bronchodilator in severe asthma with one or more severe exacerbations in the preceding year.

src.q: is indicated as add-on maintenance bronchodilator treatment in patients aged 6 years and older with severe asthma who experienced one or more severe asthma exacerbations in the preceding year

items.t: SPS: prescribe tiotropium devices and cartridges by brand name so patients get an inhaler they were trained to use.

src.q: To ensure patients receive an inhaler they have been trained to use, tiotropium capsules, cartridges and administration devices should be prescribed by brand name.

items.t: Asthma, adults: add to inhaled corticosteroids (at least 800 micrograms budesonide/day or equivalent) and at least one controller. Not a monotherapy for asthma.

src.q: In adult patients with severe asthma, tiotropium should be used in addition to inhaled corticosteroids (≥ 800 μg budesonide/day or equivalent) and at least one controller.
Spiriva Respimat should not be used as monotherapy for asthma.

items.t: Adults (COPD and asthma): 5 micrograms (two puffs) once daily at the same time each day. Do not exceed; do not use more than once daily.

src.q: The recommended dose for adults is 5 microgram tiotropium given as two puffs from the Respimat inhaler once daily, at the same time of the day. The recommended dose should not be exceeded.
Tiotropium bromide should not be used more frequently than once daily

items.t: Elderly, renal and hepatic impairment: recommended dose can be used (renal CrCl ≤ 50 ml/min: see renal).

src.q: Geriatric patients can use tiotropium bromide at the recommended dose. Renally impaired patients can use tiotropium bromide at the recommended dose.
Hepatically impaired patients can use tiotropium bromide at the recommended dose

items.t: Asthma 6-17 years: 5 micrograms (two puffs) once daily, as add-on to ICS plus controller(s) in severe asthma. Not established in moderate asthma or under 6 years. COPD: no relevant use under 18. Children should use it with an adult's help.

src.q: The recommended dose for patients 6 to 17 years of age is 5 microgram tiotropium given as two puffs from the Respimat inhaler once daily, at the same time of the day.
The safety and efficacy of Spiriva Respimat in children below 6 years of age has not been established.
There is no relevant use of Spiriva Respimat in children and adolescents below 18 years.
Children should use Spiriva Respimat with an adult's assistance.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to tiotropium, any excipient, or atropine and its derivatives (e.g. ipratropium, oxitropium).

src.q: Hypersensitivity to tiotropium bromide or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1 or to atropine or its derivatives, e.g. ipratropium or oxitropium.

items.t: Not for acute bronchospasm or symptom relief (use a rapid-acting beta-2 agonist). Not a monotherapy for asthma: keep the inhaled corticosteroid unchanged.

src.q: should not be used for the initial treatment of acute episodes of bronchospasm, or for the relief of acute symptoms. In the event of an acute attack a rapid-acting beta-2-agonist should be used.
Spiriva Respimat should not be used as monotherapy for asthma.

items.t: Anticholinergic: caution in narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hyperplasia or bladder-neck obstruction. Keep spray out of the eyes; if eye pain, blurred vision, halos or red eyes, stop and see a specialist at once.

src.q: tiotropium bromide should be used with caution in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hyperplasia or bladder-neck obstruction.
Should any combination of these eye symptoms develop, patients should stop using tiotropium bromide and consult a specialist immediately.

items.t: Cardiac: caution after MI in the last 6 months, unstable or life-threatening arrhythmia or arrhythmia needing intervention or drug change in the past year, or heart failure admission (NYHA III-IV) in the past year. MHRA: take cardiovascular risk into account and ask these patients to report worsening cardiac symptoms.

src.q: Tiotropium should be used with caution in patients with recent myocardial infarction < 6 months; any unstable or life threatening cardiac arrhythmia or cardiac arrhythmia requiring intervention or a change in drug therapy in the past year
hospitalisation of heart failure (NYHA Class III or IV) within the past year.

items.t: Renal: CrCl ≤ 50 ml/min, use only if benefit outweighs risk.

src.q: As plasma concentration increases with decreased renal function in patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance ≤ 50 ml/min) tiotropium bromide should be used only if the expected benefit outweighs the potential risk.

items.t: Not recommended in cystic fibrosis. Contains benzalkonium chloride, which may cause wheeze (higher risk in asthma). Long-term dry mouth may cause dental caries.

src.q: Spiriva Respimat is not recommended in cystic fibrosis (CF).
Benzalkonium chloride may cause wheezing and breathing difficulties. Patients with asthma are at an increased risk for these adverse events.
Dry mouth, which has been observed with anti-cholinergic treatment, may in the long term be associated with dental caries.

items.t: Other anticholinergic medicines: not studied, not recommended.

src.q: The co-administration of tiotropium bromide with other anticholinergic containing drugs has not been studied and therefore is not recommended.

items.t: Used with other common COPD and asthma medicines (sympathomimetic bronchodilators, methylxanthines, oral and inhaled steroids, antihistamines, leukotriene modifiers) without clinical evidence of interactions.

src.q: tiotropium bromide has been used concomitantly with other drugs commonly used in the treatment of COPD and asthma, including sympathomimetic bronchodilators, methylxanthines, oral and inhaled steroids, antihistamines, mucolytics, leukotriene modifiers

items.t: CrCl ≤ 50 ml/min: plasma levels rise; use only if expected benefit outweighs the risk. No long-term experience in severe renal impairment. No dose change stated.

src.q: As plasma concentration increases with decreased renal function in patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance ≤ 50 ml/min) tiotropium bromide should be used only if the expected benefit outweighs the potential risk.
There is no long term experience in patients with severe renal impairment

items.t: Hepatic impairment: recommended dose can be used.

src.q: Hepatically impaired patients can use tiotropium bromide at the recommended dose

items.t: SmPC: very limited data; as a precaution, preferably avoid in pregnancy.

src.q: There is a very limited amount of data from the use of tiotropium in pregnant women.
As a precautionary measure, it is preferable to avoid the use of Spiriva Respimat during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS (asthma): LAMAs such as tiotropium are among asthma medicines; some are less well studied, but benefits of asthma medicines usually outweigh possible risks.

src.q: Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMAs), such as tiotropium
Some asthma medications have not been as well-studied in pregnancy.

items.t: Not recommended during breastfeeding (unknown if excreted in human milk; long-acting). Decide whether to continue breastfeeding or therapy.

src.q: use of Spiriva Respimat is not recommended during breast-feeding.

items.t: Common (COPD): dry mouth (uncommon in asthma). Other effects are uncommon or rarer: dizziness, headache, cough, pharyngitis, dysphonia, constipation, oral candidiasis, rash, pruritus; in COPD also urinary retention and dysuria.

src.q: Serious undesirable effects consistent with anticholinergic effects include glaucoma, constipation, intestinal obstruction including ileus paralytic and urinary retention.

items.t: Immediate hypersensitivity (angioedema, anaphylaxis) and inhalation-induced bronchospasm can occur.

src.q: Immediate hypersensitivity reactions may occur after administration of tiotropium bromide inhalation solution.

items.t: Once a day, two puffs each time. Insert the cartridge and prime until a cloud appears, then 3 more puffs. If unused for more than 7 days, release one puff to the ground; if more than 21 days, prime again. Use the reusable inhaler for no more than one year (up to 6 cartridges).
